causes: The blended palette has no white and no black, so dark, muted and pale colours cannot be reached and the nearest is used instead.
colours came out wrong.looks: Blended colours print brighter, paler or simply different from what the model specified.

causes: The model is larger than the target printer's build volume, which is easy to miss when a file was made for a bigger machine.
does not fit the plate.looks: The slicer refuses the model, or silently places it hanging off the plate.

causes: The nozzle is slightly too close to the plate on the first layer.
The bed is hotter than the material needs, keeping the base soft.
elephant foot.looks: The bottom one or two layers bulge out wider than the rest of the part.
elephant foot.note: Prism cannot see this: it is first layer calibration, not a project setting.

causes: An overhang that had no support under it, so the first layer over thin air curled up and the nozzle struck it.
Supports that were generated but too thin or too tall to stay standing.
The part came away from the plate, usually a corner lifting first.
failed partway up.looks: The print goes well for hours and then a section collapses, or the part detaches and the printer carries on extruding into air.

causes: The nozzle struck something, usually a curled overhang or a knocked-over support, and the belt skipped.
A mechanical problem: loose belt, binding rail, or a pulley grub screw.
layer shifts.looks: The print continues but everything above a certain height is offset sideways.
layer shifts.note: If it happens at the same height every time, look at the model. If it happens at random heights, look at the printer.

causes: Walls, infill and solid layers stacked up by cautious defaults nobody revisited.
Layer height left fine when the model does not need it.
Ironing on over large flat areas.
print is too slow.looks: A small model quotes many hours.

causes: Not enough solid layers on top to bridge the gaps in the infill below.
Infill too sparse, so the solid layers have too far to span.
Too little cooling, so the strands sag before they set.
rough or pillowing top.looks: The top face is lumpy, or has small holes, as though it did not quite close over.

causes: Damp filament, which is by far the most common cause and gets worse over weeks in an open room.
Retraction too short or too slow.
Nozzle temperature higher than the filament needs.
stringing.looks: Fine threads strung between separate parts of the print.
stringing.note: Prism cannot see this in your file. It is a filament and hardware matter: dry the spool first, before changing any setting.

causes: The vertical gap between support and model is too small, so the two fused.
No interface layers, so the model printed straight onto sparse support lines and keyed into them.
supports will not come off.looks: The supports are welded to the part and come away only with pliers, taking surface with them.

causes: Every layer has to start and stop somewhere, so the seam always exists. The question is only where it goes and whether it is aligned.
visible seam.looks: A vertical line of blobs or a groove running up the part where each layer started.
visible seam.note: This one cannot be removed, only placed. Aligned puts it in a straight line you can hide or sand.

causes: The part cooled unevenly, shrinking as it went. ABS, ASA and PETG do this far more than PLA.
Too much part cooling for the material.
A plate that is not clean. Skin oils are the usual culprit.
warping.looks: Corners peel up from the plate, and the base ends up curved.

causes: Too much cooling, which stops each layer welding properly to the one below.
Too few walls. Adding walls strengthens a part more efficiently than adding infill.
Printed in an orientation that puts the load across the layers rather than along them.
weak or brittle parts.looks: The part breaks along a layer line under modest load.
